clue.text: Part of book that may come out in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a supplementary section at the back of a book

definitions.text: that may come out in the theatre
definitions.meaning: the vestigial organ surgeons remove in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: Something from a book that might pop up during a stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests a stage, but here it is the operating theatre, where an inflamed organ is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same word: back matter in a book and the small gut organ removed in surgery.

clue.text: Perhaps Egyptian's day in a prison

indicators.note: in means the day goes inside the other letters

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

explanation.surface: An Egyptian's single day locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is on the continent of Africa, so an Egyptian is an example of a person from there.

clue.text: Publicity about period radio device

indicators.note: about means the publicity letters go around the period

parts.note: PR is public relations, i.e. publicity
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A news item about a bygone wireless gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager, or bleeper, is a small radio receiver that alerts its wearer.

clue.text: Holiday camp that is barely visited

definitions.text: Holiday camp that is barely visited

parts.words: Holiday camp that is barely visited
parts.note: barely suggests hardly anyone goes, but means the guests wear no clothes

explanation.surface: An unpopular resort that gets almost no guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist resort is a camp where visitors go about naked, bare.

clue.text: I count as angry

parts.note: to rate something is to count or regard it as such

explanation.surface: Someone declares they qualify as cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean furious or cross.

clue.text: Shortly announce a piece of data

indicators.note: said shortly, the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: to announce is to state

explanation.surface: Someone briefly declares a single fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon' but tells you to drop the last letter of STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat is an informal short form of statistic, a single figure or item of data.

clue.text: Take liberty to see if dress fits

definitions.meaning: to attempt something cheeky to see if one gets away with it
to put on a garment to test it

explanation.surface: A shopper presumes to test a frock in the changing room.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to test someone's tolerance and also to wear clothing on a trial basis.

clue.text: Those people's time with the next in line

parts.note: an heir is next in line to inherit

explanation.surface: Some family spends time with its successor.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a group of others, belonging to them.

clue.text: Assess price of electrical connection to be very expensive

parts.note: to cost something is to estimate its price
the earth, in British usage, is the ground wire of an electrical circuit

explanation.surface: An electrician prices up a ground wire and finds it pricey.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to require a huge sum of money.

clue.text: Stiff outfit I had

parts.note: a rig, or rig-out, is an outfit of clothes
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls wearing an uncomfortably starchy costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe something that will not bend.

clue.text: Wildly annoyed — relieving drug found

indicators.note: the letters of annoyed are thrown about wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: A furious patient finally gets hold of a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a medicine that eases pain, a painkiller.

clue.text: Dog old police force rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the force's initials are read backwards

parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001

explanation.surface: A police dog is turned away by the former constabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel or worthless dog, a specific kind of the general term.

clue.text: Magazine I'm not involved in?

definitions.meaning: A long-running British weekly political magazine
what an onlooker might say: someone who watches but takes no part

explanation.surface: A journalist distances themselves from a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher at an event is uninvolved, and the same name belongs to a London weekly periodical.

clue.text: Signify assent, given sweet dessert? Negative reply

parts.note: to nod the head is to signal yes
an ice is a frozen sweet, ice cream or sorbet

explanation.surface: Someone agrees when offered pudding, then asks whether it is actually refused.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No dice' is an idiom for a refusal, meaning no luck or no deal.

clue.text: Expert wrong to pick up cards

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means lifting so the word reads upwards, reversed

parts.note: bad means wrong
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

explanation.surface: A skilled player is mistaken to gather up the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a British idiom for a skilled person, an adept.

clue.text: Tucking hard into alcohol, daughter complained peevishly

indicators.note: tucking something into another word places it inside
into completes the instruction, naming the word that takes the letter

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A daughter tucking into the drink grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking ... into' puts H inside WINE, giving WHINE, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine is to complain in a querulous, petulant way; the past tense matches.

clue.text: Glad it can be twisted round one of the fingers

indicators.note: twisted round means the letters of glad it, plus the extra letter, are wound into another order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that a ring can be turned on a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted round' looks like it describes the ring; it shuffles GLADIT with I (one) added.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to the digits of the hand.

clue.text: Injured Cuban, lame, collected in this?

definitions.text: Injured Cuban, lame, collected in this?

indicators.note: injured suggests the letters of the two words are damaged and reformed

explanation.surface: A hurt and limping Cuban is picked up by an emergency vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: an injured lame person would be collected in this vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency vehicle is what picks up the injured and takes them to hospital.

clue.text: Permitted to remove top, very bad

indicators.note: removing the top means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: lawful means permitted by law

explanation.surface: Being allowed to take off one's top is outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean dreadful or terrible.

clue.text: Are they found in top of tree in loch?

definitions.text: Are they found in top of tree in loch?

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the loch's name

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

indicators.note: the top of a down entry word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A query about whether birds' homes sit high in trees by a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: birds' homes are found at the tops of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds build their homes, often high in trees.

clue.text: Joker, one accompanying a footballer

definitions.meaning: ..., wives and girlfriends, is British tabloid slang for footballers' partners

explanation.surface: A comedian goes along with a football star.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorist is a wag, and British tabloids call a footballer's wife or girlfriend a WAG.

clue.text: Carried on having weekly-paid job

definitions.meaning: conducted, as in carrying on a war or campaign
earning a wage, in paid employment

explanation.surface: Someone kept going in a job paid by the week.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is conducting a war or campaign; the other describes a worker earning wages.

clue.text: Shows off extremely faithful relatives

indicators.note: extremely means only the outer letters of faithful are used

parts.note: aunts are family relatives

explanation.surface: Loyal family members parade themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to display ostentatiously, a synonym of showing off.

clue.text: Entitlement, OK?

definitions.meaning: a claim one is entitled to
a tag asking for agreement, as in 'all set, yes?'

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a claim is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a just claim and also serves as a query seeking assent.

clue.text: Cover over swimming pool

parts.note: a lid is a cover
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Instructions to cover up a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: In old heaps, wild flower

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of old heaps are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wildflower grows among old rubbish heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family plant, an example of a flower, linked in myth with the underworld.
